findings.fact: South holds only DA and DK in diamonds; West has led DQ.
findings.explanation: South cannot duck this diamond trick regardless of East’s card. Either legal diamond play wins, so the proposed conditional duck is physically impossible.
quotes: At South’s turn, duck the first round if East’s card and the position make that safe; otherwise take a diamond honor.

findings.fact: The current trick is DQ–D3–D4, and South holds DA and DK.
findings.explanation: DA wins the trick and leaves DK as a stopper. Developing clubs is feasible, with HK providing an available dummy entry.
quotes: Take the diamond with the ace, retaining the king as a second stopper. Then develop clubs, preserving entries to dummy where possible, and count the remaining tricks before pursuing overtricks.

findings.fact: South holds CAK864 opposite CQ72, with HK available as a dummy entry and DK retained.
findings.explanation: Leading C4 begins a feasible club-development route consistent with the retained plan.
quotes: With the trick complete, lead a club from hand to establish the suit while retaining the diamond king as a stopper.

findings.fact: West has played C9 over South’s C4; dummy holds CQ72. Declarer has five side-suit winners counting the diamond already won.
findings.explanation: Ducking is a sound safety route: conceding a club can establish four club tricks even against a 4–1 break. CQ remains usable through the available HK entry, and no unknown defensive holding is asserted.
quotes: Dummy should play low under West’s C9, preserving the queen to cover a later lower club lead.
